questions.q: What does terraform init actually do?
options: Creates all the resources declared in your configuration immediately
Deletes the current terraform.tfstate file and starts over
Downloads required providers into .terraform/, sets up the state backend, and writes .terraform.lock.hcl
Only validates HCL syntax without touching providers or state
questions.explain: init prepares the working directory: it downloads provider plugins matching your version constraints, sets up where state will be stored, and locks the resolved provider version.

questions.q: Why is terraform plan described as a 'dry run'?
options: It automatically applies only the lowest-risk changes and skips the rest
It only works after terraform apply has already run once
It shows what would change without actually creating, updating, or destroying anything in your cloud
It deletes resources that are no longer in the configuration
questions.explain: plan diffs your declared configuration against state (refreshed from the real API) and shows the resulting actions, but never touches your actual cloud resources.

questions.q: In Terraform plan output, what does a `~` next to an attribute mean?
options: That attribute is new and will be created for the first time
That attribute will be permanently deleted
That attribute caused a syntax error and will be ignored
That attribute will be updated in place, without destroying and recreating the resource
questions.explain: ~ marks an in-place update — the resource itself is not destroyed, only the changed attribute is updated.

questions.q: What happens when you run terraform apply and are shown the confirmation prompt?
options: Typing 'no' still partially applies the safest changes
Only typing 'yes' proceeds with the plan; anything else cancels and nothing changes
Pressing Enter with no input automatically approves the plan
The prompt is cosmetic and apply proceeds regardless of what you type
questions.explain: The confirmation prompt is a real safety feature — only an explicit 'yes' approves the actions; any other input cancels with no changes made.

questions.q: After terraform apply successfully creates a resource, where does Terraform record what it now manages?
options: It only logs the result to the console, with no persistent record
It writes the result into the state file, terraform.tfstate
It stores the result inside the .terraform.lock.hcl file
It emails the resource group details to the account owner
questions.explain: Terraform writes the outcome of apply back into terraform.tfstate, which becomes the record it diffs against on the next plan or apply.
